name: Council of Basel-Ferrara-Florence
summary: The Council of Basel-Ferrara-Florence-Rome (1431–1449) is the last great conciliarist council and the arena of the final confrontation between papal authority and the Conciliar movement. Basel initially issues the radical decree Sacrosancta (1432) asserting council superiority over the pope. Pope Eugene IV attempts to dissolve Basel and move the council to Ferrara (1437) for Greek union negotiations. The rump council at Basel deposes Eugene (1439) and elects the antipope Felix V, the last antipope in Church history. Felix V resigns in 1449; Basel collapses. The failure of the Basel conciliarists permanently restores papal supremacy over councils.

_quarry.structural_significance: Final confrontation between Conciliarism and papal monarchy; papal victory at Basel-Florence permanently ends the conciliarist challenge; Felix V (1439–1449) is the last antipope in history; the council's failure leaves church reform unresolved until the Protestant Reformation
